title: Unbounded finite-free image comparisons with their finite-sum normalization
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a map of finite commutative rings, with $B$ free of finite rank $r$ over $A$. For a scheme $W$ use the ordinary small etale module derived categories, $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB$, and exact restriction $U_W$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $f:V\to W$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For every unbounded $B$-complex $N$, the canonical restriction comparison is an isomorphism
$$U_WRf_{*,B}N\cong Rf_{*,A}U_VN.$$
For every unbounded $K\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the projection comparison
$$c_{f,K}:T_WRf_{*,A}K\longrightarrow Rf_{*,B}T_VK$$
is a natural isomorphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Its transpose under $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ is the extended $A$-counit, using the canonical pullback/tensor identification. Under any basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B/A$ and the displayed restriction identification, $U_Wc_{f,K}$ is precisely the finite-sum map $(Rf_{*,A}K)^{\oplus r}\to Rf_{*,A}(K^{\oplus r})$ whose $j$-th component is $Rf_{*,A}$ of $k\mapsto k\otimes b_j$. Its inverse is given by $Rf_{*,A}$ of the corresponding projections. These assertions impose no cohomological-dimension or boundedness hypothesis.

If $f$ has a chosen compactification $V\xrightarrow j\overline V\xrightarrow p W$ with $j$ open and $p$ proper and the schemes Noetherian, put $F_R=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ for $R=A,B$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The canonical maps $T_{\overline V}j_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T_V$ and $U_{\overline V}j_{!,B}\cong j_{!,A}U_V$ agree with $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes b$ on the open and with the unique zero maps off it. Consequently $U_WF_B\cong F_AU_V$ and
$$c^!_f:T_WF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_V.$$
After restriction, $c^!_f$ is again exactly the finite-sum map, with components $F_A$ of the basis inclusions. This includes a structure morphism to a field and a closed immersion as $f$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: ordinary direct-image projection comparison by additivity and the compact-support counit; returned proof steps 4-5

proof.text: Fix a basis and its coefficient maps $b_j:A\to B$, $\lambda_j:B\to A$. For a module sheaf $M$ set $i_j(m)=m\otimes b_j$ and $p_j(m\otimes b)=\lambda_j(b)m$. The tensor/sheafification universal properties give $p_ji_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\sum_ji_jp_j=1$, hence $U(M\otimes_A B)\cong M^{\oplus r}$ naturally in $M$. In particular scalar extension $E=-\otimes_A B$ is exact: after the conservative, exact $U$ it is a finite direct sum of identity functors. The sectionwise tensor adjunction, whose inverse is $h\mapsto(m\otimes b\mapsto bh(m))$, respects restrictions and sheafifies, so $E\dashv U$. Exact-functor derivation identifies $T$ with termwise $E$ on every complex. The same coordinate equations hold there. Also $U$ on derived categories reflects isomorphisms: the cone of a map has zero cohomology if its underlying scalar-restricted complex does, because $U$ is exact and conservative.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; tensor coordinates, with Tag 05DQ (algebra.tex, lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict)

proof.text: For $N$ choose a $B$-K-injective resolution $N\to I$. Since $E\dashv U$ and $E$ is exact by step 1, restriction $UI$ is $A$-K-injective. The ordinary direct-image formula on each etale test object is the same section module with its action restricted; consequently $U_Wf_{*,B}I=f_{*,A}U_VI$. Both sides compute the unbounded derived functors, giving the canonical natural isomorphism $d_N:U_WRf_{*,B}N\xrightarrow\sim Rf_{*,A}U_VN$. The comparison also respects the geometric adjunctions: termwise the two Hom bijections are the same underlying sheaf-adjunction bijection, since inverse image restricts the coefficient action and its unit and counit are the underlying abelian-sheaf ones. Direct images of $I$ and $UI$ are also K-injective, by the same right-adjoint lemma applied to the exact inverse images. On these K-injective targets, the homotopy-to-derived Hom bijections transport exactly this identity. Thus restricting the $B$-adjunct of $t:f_B^*M\to N$ and then applying $d_N$ gives the $A$-adjunct of $U(t)$, with $f_A^*UM\cong Uf_B^*M$. These statements hold for arbitrary unbounded $M,N$.

source.place: Tags 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); ordinary etale adjunction as in the cited node

proof.text: The functor $Rf_{*,A}$ is additive. Indeed a morphism into a K-injective representative is its unique homotopy class; direct image is additive on these classes, and localization is additive. For a finite direct sum of K-injectives, maps from an acyclic complex are the finite direct sum of zero Hom groups, so the sum is K-injective and computes the direct image of the sum. Alternatively, applying additivity directly to $\pi_ji_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\sum i_j\pi_j=1$ proves that the canonical finite-sum comparison is invertible, with inverse the family $Rf_{*,A}(\pi_j)$. This also proves the assertion for the empty sum.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula, finite-free reduction; finite biproduct equations written explicitly

proof.text: The canonical pullback/tensor isomorphism $f_B^*T_W\cong T_Vf_A^*$ is induced on sheaves by $f^{-1}(m\otimes b)\mapsto f^{-1}m\otimes b$; its inverse is the inverse-image tensor comparison. Since all four functors here are exact, the same isomorphism on complexes gives the displayed derived identification. Define $c_{f,K}$ to be the $B$-adjunct of $T_V(\varepsilon_{f,A,K})$ after this identification. This is the coefficient projection comparison: it has the prescribed extended-counit transpose, just as the fixed-coefficient projection morphism is the adjunct of counit tensored with identity. Naturality follows by applying the natural adjunction bijection to the natural extended counit.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: the ordinary direct-image projection comparison; explicit extended-counit normalization

proof.text: Put $L=Rf_{*,A}K$. Let $i_j:L\to U_WT_WL$ and $i'_j:K\to U_VT_VK$ be the basis inclusions of step 1. By the compatibility of adjunctions in step 2, the transpose of $d_{T_VK}\,U_W(c_{f,K})\,i_j$ is $i'_j\varepsilon_{f,A,K}$: the pullback/tensor map of step 4 sends its $j$-th basis vector to the same $b_j$. Naturality of the $A$-counit says that the transpose of $Rf_{*,A}(i'_j)$ is also $i'_j\varepsilon_{f,A,K}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore identifies the two columns. The maps $\lambda_j$ give projections $p'_j:U_VT_VK\to K$. Step 3 and the equations $p'_ji'_k=\delta_{jk}$, $\sum i'_jp'_j=1$ show that the row $\bigl(Rf_{*,A}(p'_j)\bigr)_j$ is the inverse of this comparison. Since $d$ is invertible and $U_W$ reflects isomorphisms by step 1, $c_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism. This proves precisely the claimed normalization for every chosen basis, without asserting that basis inclusions themselves are $B$-linear.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: additivity for a finite free coefficient module; columns and inverse computed from the extended counit

proof.text: For the open immersion $j$, the presheaves defining $U_{\overline V}j_{!,B}N$ and $j_{!,A}U_VN$ have exactly the same abelian groups and maps: they are $N(S\to V)$ when $S$ factors through the open and zero otherwise. Module sheafification has the same underlying abelian sheaf in both coefficient categories, so these give a natural isomorphism $e:U_{\overline V}j_{!,B}\cong j_{!,A}U_V$. Exactness of both open extensions and of restriction makes it the same comparison on arbitrary complexes. For tensor extension use the isomorphism $q:T_{\overline V}j_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T_V$ of the cited open-tensor lemma. Its ordinary map is the balanced map $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes b$ on the open and zero off it, and it has that same normalization in the derived categories. In particular $e\,U(q)$ carries the $j$-th inclusion $j_{!,A}K\to U T_{\overline V}j_{!,A}K$ to $j_{!,A}(i'_j)$: this is the equality of those presheaf maps on the open and on the zero terms, followed by sheafification and localization.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); scalar tensor normalization as in lem-coef-etale-open-tensor

proof.text:
For the chosen compactification apply step 2 to $p$ and then step 6 to $j$. This gives $U_WF_B\cong Rp_{*,A}U_{\overline V}j_{!,B}\cong F_AU_V$. Define $c_f^!$ by the composite
$$T_WRp_{*,A}j_{!,A}\xrightarrow{c_p}Rp_{*,B}T_{\overline V}j_{!,A}\xrightarrow{Rp_{*,B}(q)}Rp_{*,B}j_{!,B}T_V.$$
Each arrow is an isomorphism by steps 5 and 6. Under the displayed restriction comparison, its $j$-th column is $Rp_{*,A}(e\,U(q))\,Rp_{*,A}(i_j)=Rp_{*,A}(j_{!,A}(i'_j))=F_A(i'_j)$, by naturality of step 2 and the column equality in step 6. The inverse is the row $F_A(p'_j)$, since $F_A$ is additive as a composite of additive functors and the coordinate equations are unchanged. This is exactly the requested finite-sum normalization. No use was made of boundedness or finite cohomological dimension. Structure morphisms to fields and closed immersions with the stated compactifications are included by specialization; no assertion of existence of a compactification for an arbitrary scheme morphism is needed.
